subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What name is often given to the cultural flourishing of Elizabeth's reign?
questions.explain: The Elizabethan era is often called a 'Golden Age' for its achievements in theatre, exploration and the arts.

questions.q: What was a key cause of rising poverty and vagrancy in Elizabethan England?
options: A long period of peace abroad
Population growth, inflation and enclosure of land
The decline of the wool trade only
questions.explain: Rising population, inflation, enclosure and unemployment all increased poverty and the numbers of vagrants.

questions.q: The poorest theatre-goers who stood in the open yard of the Globe were nicknamed what?
questions.explain: 'Groundlings' paid the lowest price and stood in the open yard around the stage.

questions.q: The Elizabethan Poor Law of 1601 made which body responsible for caring for the poor?
questions.explain: The 1601 Poor Law made each parish responsible for its own poor, funded by a local poor rate.

questions.q: What was the main feature of Elizabeth's Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Union of the English and Scottish churches
A 'middle way' Protestant Church with Elizabeth as Supreme Governor
questions.explain: The 1559 Settlement created a moderate Protestant Church with Elizabeth as Supreme Governor, seeking a compromise between Catholics and Protestants.

questions.q: In which year did the Spanish Armada attempt to invade England?
questions.explain: The Spanish Armada sailed against England in 1588 and was defeated.

questions.q: Plays in Elizabethan theatres were performed at what time of day?
questions.explain: Open-air theatres like the Globe relied on natural light, so plays were staged in the afternoon.

questions.q: Who was Elizabeth I's trusted Secretary of State and chief adviser for much of her reign?
questions.explain: William Cecil (Lord Burghley) served as Elizabeth's principal adviser for decades.

questions.q: Which event is associated with Elizabeth's speech promising she had the 'heart and stomach of a king'?
options: The Tilbury speech during the Armada of 1588
The opening of the Globe in 1599
questions.explain: Elizabeth gave her famous speech to the troops at Tilbury in 1588 as the Armada threatened.

questions.q: What was the recusancy fine, introduced under Elizabeth, a punishment for?
options: Refusing to attend Church of England services
Failing to pay the poor rate
questions.explain: Recusants were people, mostly Catholics, fined for refusing to attend the official Protestant church services.

questions.q: Who was the first Englishman to circumnavigate the globe, returning in 1580?
questions.explain: Francis Drake completed his circumnavigation of the world in 1580 aboard the Golden Hind.

questions.q: The Act of Uniformity of 1559 required the use of which book in church services?
options: A new Book of Common Prayer
questions.explain: The 1559 Act of Uniformity imposed a revised English Book of Common Prayer on all parishes.

questions.q: Who commanded the Spanish Armada that sailed against England in 1588?
questions.explain: The Duke of Medina Sidonia was appointed to command the Spanish Armada in 1588.

questions.q: Mary, Queen of Scots, fled to England in 1568 after defeat at which battle?
questions.explain: Mary fled to England in 1568 after her forces were defeated at the Battle of Langside near Glasgow.

questions.q: In which year did the Pope excommunicate Elizabeth I, encouraging Catholics to oppose her?
questions.explain: Pope Pius V excommunicated Elizabeth in 1570, releasing Catholics from allegiance to her.

questions.q: Why was Elizabeth's refusal to marry a problem for England?
options: It threatened a clear Protestant succession
It started a war with France
questions.explain: Without a child, the succession was uncertain, raising fears of a Catholic claimant taking the throne.

questions.q: Mary, Queen of Scots, was executed in 1587 after her involvement in which plot?
questions.explain: The Babington Plot of 1586 implicated Mary in a scheme to assassinate Elizabeth, leading to Mary's execution in 1587.

questions.q: In what year did Elizabeth I become Queen of England?
questions.explain: Elizabeth I acceded to the throne in 1558 following the death of her half-sister Mary I.

questions.q: Which London theatre, associated with Shakespeare, opened in 1599?
questions.explain: The Globe Theatre opened in 1599 and was home to Shakespeare's company.

questions.q: Which Englishman organised and sponsored the failed colony at Roanoke in the New World?
questions.explain: Sir Walter Raleigh organised and sponsored the Roanoke colony under a royal patent from Elizabeth I, though he did not sail there himself; the colonists vanished, becoming the 'Lost Colony'.

questions.q: Which half-sister did Elizabeth I succeed when she became queen in 1558?
questions.explain: Elizabeth succeeded her Catholic half-sister Mary I, who died in November 1558.

questions.q: Sir Francis Walsingham is best known for running Elizabeth's network of what?
questions.explain: Walsingham ran an extensive spy network that uncovered Catholic plots against Elizabeth.
